SUBJECT: REVIEW LAS POSADAS EVENT AMENITIES AND FOOD TASTING

Background:

Las Posadas began many years ago and concluded in 2010 with a final event. Councilmember
Margarita Rios submitted a special request to bring back the program during Fiscal Year 2017-
2018. Since then, the department has continued to offer this cultural program for the Norwalk
community.
Las Posadas is an event that kicks off the New Year with the Recreation and Park Services
Department (RPSD), with the first special event of the year, Las Posadas 2026. This event
features a distribution of more than 1,000 tamales and cups of hot chocolate. Guests will enjoy
various activities, including craft stations and the distribution of 500 candy bags. Live
entertainment and a folkloric dance will highlight the evening. Additionally, attendees will browse
unique offerings from several night market vendors and food trucks, creating a vibrant, festive
celebration.

Fiscal Impact:

The RPSD allocated budget for Las Posadas in Fiscal Year 2025-2026 is $21,411 under the
account 101-50-5610, which includes personnel and operating expenditures.

SUBJECT: REVIEW EVENT ELEMENTS AND VOLUNTEER OPPORTUNITIES FOR
  ARTASTIC 2026

Background:

The City of Norwalk’s Recreation and Park Services Department (RPSD) successfully hosted
the 2025 Artastic, Art Festival, and Student Art Competition event on March 14, 2025. This event
celebrates the arts and highlight the Cultural Arts Center’s programs and classes. This
community event features free art activities and projects, multiple art exhibits, entertainment,
while promoting community connection and family-friendly recreational opportunities within the
city. RPSD is currently exploring event elements to add to the 2026 Artastic event scheduled for
Friday, March 20, 2026, and is requesting recommendations from the Parks and Recreation
Commission.

Along with event element recommendations, there are several volunteer opportunities open to
City Commissioners. See the list below:

  •  Artastic Community Art Competition & Scholarship Program
  Celebrates local middle and high school artists in the Artastic art competition. This year
  will mark the 15th Annual Community Art Competition and Scholarship Program.
  Students’ work will be on display from March 18-20, 2026. A total of $600 in
  scholarships will be awarded to the top artists at the Artastic event being held on Friday,
  March 20, 2026.

  This portion of the event would require two (2) judges from the Parks and Recreation
  Commission to collaborate with the Arts in Public Places Commission.
 Parks and Rec Commission Meeting  November 13, 2025
Review Event Elements and Volunteer Opportunities  Page No. 2
for Artastic 2026

  •  Community Chalk Art Competition
  This contest is part of the Artastic event at the Cultural Arts Center. Pre-registration is
  required. A 10-piece set of non-toxic pastels (chalk) will be provided to all registered
  artists. Prizes will be given to the top-placing artists. There are three categories: 8-13
  years, 14 & over, and Professional Artist.

  This portion of the event would require four (4) judges from the Parks and Recreation
  Commission.

  •  Drum Circle
  This portion of the event will highlight the art of music. This will be an interactive, hands-
  on activity. There will be a lead instructor who organizes the drumming and percussion
  instruments.

  This portion of the event would require volunteers to help distribute musical instruments
  to the children and/or assist them in finding an available drum.

RPSD is requesting confirmation for all City Commissioners interested in volunteering for the
event by January 8, 2026.

Fiscal Impact:

The RPSD allocated budget for 2026 Artastic in Fiscal Year 2025-2026 is $25,034 under the
account 101-50-5614, which includes personnel and operating expenditures.

Citizens Advised:

N/A

Strategic Plan 2023-2025 Implementation:

Goal No. 1 – Provide High Quality Customer Service to the Community

Recommended Action:

Staff recommends that the Parks and Recreation Commission:
a. Provide event element recommendations for the 2026 Artastic event; and

b. Confirm Commissioner volunteer participation by January 8, 2026.

SUBJECT: REVIEW OF THE 2026 SUMMER CONCERT AND FRONT
  STREET FRIDAY NIGHT SERIES

Background:

The City of Norwalk’s Recreation and Park Services Department (RPSD) successfully hosted
the 2025 Summer Concert series and Front Street Friday Nights series between July and August
2025. These events were designed to promote community connection, highlight local talent, and
encourage family-friendly recreation opportunities within the City.

The Summer Concert Series took place on Wednesday evenings from July 9 through August 6,
2025, at Norwalk Park, offering free live entertainment, food vendors, and children’s activities.
Each concert averaged over 900 attendees, with the Chamber expo averaging over 1300
attendees. The total estimated attendance was 3,100 over the course of the series.

The 2025 concert lineup featured a variety of genres appealing to all ages:

 Date  Performer  Genre
 July 3  Undercover  Top 40
 July 9  Grupo Neblina  Latin
 July 23  Blue Breeze  Motown/Funk
 August 6  Soto Band  Top 40/Old school
 Parks and Recreation Commission Meeting  November 13, 2025
Review the 2026 Summer Concert and Front Street  Page No. 3
Friday Night Series

The Front Street Friday Nights series was held on every other Friday of the week (July through
August) along the Historic Front Street. Each event featured live music, classic car displays,
local vendors, and food trucks. Average attendance was approximately 1,000–1,500 attendees
per event, totaling 3,800 attendees.

Both event series received overwhelmingly positive feedback from attendees and vendors,
citing improved layout, sound quality, and family-friendly programming. The 2025 Front Street
Friday lineup was as follows:

 Date  Performer  Genre
 July 18  The Romantics  Taylor Swift tribute (pop)
 August 1  Bruno and The  R&B
  Hooligans
 August 15  Latin Soul  Cumbias

The Recreation and Park Services Department is currently planning the 2026 Summer Concert
and Front Street Friday series and is requesting recommendations from the Parks and
Recreation Commission as it relates to music genres for each concert night.

Fiscal Impact:

The Summer Concert Series and Front Street Friday Night series were funded through the
Recreation and Park Services Department’s Special Events budget.

Staff recommend the Parks and Recreation Commission assist in recommending the genres for

SUBJECT: REVIEW THE 2026 SPECIAL EVENTS CALENDAR

Background:

The City of Norwalk Recreation and Park Services Department (RPSD) has drafted the 2026
Special Events Calendar. The calendar is a listing of pre-approved and budgeted events and
programs under RPSD, as well as Recreation-supported events led by other City departments,
including Communications, City Administration, Human Resources, and Social Services. The list
also includes internal staff events, training, and conferences for scheduling purposes. This
calendar is not a public document nor a comprehensive list of all City of Norwalk events. For a
master list of all City events, the public may access and download the Community Calendar
located at www.norwalkca.gov/calendar and filter by Department.

The 2026 Special Events Calendar may be updated throughout the year as operational and
budgetary needs change. Event itineraries, fliers, and additional event-related documents for
major City events will continue to be emailed to Parks and Recreation Commissioners two weeks
before each event. Commissioners may also reach out to the Commission Liaison, who is the
Director of Recreation and Park Services, for any additional questions or information.
